claims.assertion: The driver did arrive and was within 200 m of the pickup: GPS puts the closest approach at 36 m at 17:15:00, first inside 200 m at 17:14:35, and stationary 40 m from the pickup from 17:15:05 to 17:22:55, so NS-1(i) is satisfied.

The driver pressed 'I'm Here' at 17:15:05 and stayed within 200 m for 7 min 50 s afterwards with no GPS gap, so NS-1(iv) continuous presence is satisfied and no TH-4 escalation for missing GPS is available.
The driver sent 2 in-app messages (first 17:15:35) and made 1 in-app call (17:16:35, not answered), satisfying NS-1(iii)'s one-message-and-one-call requirement — a condition I concede on the record.

The free-wait condition is not met on the clock the record supports: the record threshold is 8 minutes, and although cancellation at 17:22:55 is 7 min 50 s after the 17:15:05 arrival it is 10 min 55 s after the 17:12:00 acceptance, while NS-1(ii) counts from the later of scheduled pickup time and arrival and no scheduled pickup time appears in the record — the condition is therefore undecidable from the records produced.

The driver's own written statement relies on 'the full 8 minutes the rule gives' yet he cancelled 7 min 50 s after tapping 'I'm Here' (and 10 min 55 s after acceptance), so his account of having waited the full threshold is contradicted by the timeline and GPS records, which win over a statement.

The driver's second message at 17:22 — '8 min up, cancelling the trip' — shows he treated the 8-minute mark as not yet reached and then cancelled before it, which is the opposite of the rider no-show the app reason records.

Because the free-wait threshold was not demonstrably satisfied before the driver cancelled, the $5.00 cancellation fee fails the only chargeable condition (NS-1) and must be refunded in full under NS-2; the fee on record is $5.00 and surge is 1.0× so no other element is in issue.

The driver profile carries 1 upheld dispute in 90 days, on a no-show, against 1291 trips; profile facts cannot decide the case but support a note on the driver's cancellation practice rather than any penalty on the rider.

weaknesses: My client's own complaint is only that she came out 'a minute after' the cancellation, so the record shows she did not come out during the wait; the other side will use F13 (call at 17:16 unanswered) and F5 to argue she was uncontactable throughout.

The 8-minute threshold in NS-1(ii) is not spelled out in this case's records; the other side will read F3/F6/F7 (arrival 17:15:05, cancellation 17:22:55 = 7 min 50 s) together with the driver's statement F14 ('waited the full 8 minutes') and argue the wait requirement was met, making the timing claim in C4 look like an over-reading.
NS-1(iii) is satisfied on the record (F5, F13), so my defence does not rest on any failure to contact — I can only attack the wait condition.
There is no scheduled pickup time in the fact index, so the other side can argue the later-of-two rule collapses to arrival and the fee stands.

claims.assertion: The driver was at the pickup point: GPS puts his closest approach at 36 m (F1), first entry within 200 m of the pickup at 17:14:35 (F2), stationary 40 m from the pickup from 17:15:05 until cancellation (F3), satisfying the 200 m arrival radius.
Arrival was recorded in-app: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 17:15:05, 40 m from the pickup point, and stayed within 200 m for the following 7 min 50 s (F7, F6).

The free wait was exhausted: the record's no-show threshold is 8 minutes, and the driver cancelled at 17:22:55, 7 min 50 s after the recorded arrival at 17:15:05 and 10 min 55 s after acceptance at 17:12:00 — past the later-of-two wait on any reading (F4, F6).
The contact conditions were met before cancellation: the driver sent 2 in-app messages, the first at 17:15:35, and made 1 in-app call at 17:16:35, all before he cancelled at 17:22:55 (F5, F13).

The driver's chat shows he gave the rider notice and waited, not an errand or an abandonment: "I'm here at the pickup point, white Honda Vezel." at 17:15 and "8 min up, cancelling the trip" at 17:22, the latter exactly matching the record's 8-minute no-show threshold (F10, F11, F12, F4).

The driver's stated reason matches the record: the app reason is rider_no_show and his statement says he pressed "I'm Here" and waited the full 8 minutes, so this is a no-show cancellation under NS-1/NS-2, not a driver-side cancellation under NS-3 (F4, F14).

The rider's complaint that she "came out a minute after the driver cancelled" is not corroborated by any system record: the driver stayed stationary at 40 m from the pickup for the whole 7 min 50 s wait and there is no record of the rider ever approaching or messaging (F3, F12, F10, F11).
The charge is the fixed $5.00 no-show fee with no surge component (1.0×), so on the upheld record the fee stands in full and no refund of any part is due (F8, F9).
The $5.00 fixed-sum cancellation dispute is decided by the system as final under TH-2/TH-1, so no human referral or escalation is warranted here (F8, F4).

The driver's profile shows 6.5 years on the platform with no route deviation history; his single prior upheld dispute is a no-show dispute, which is background only and does not decide this case or support a flag under RD-6/NS-1 (F19).

weaknesses: Clause NS-1 uses a 5-minute free wait from the later of scheduled pickup time and arrival, while the 8-minute threshold comes from the record; if the judge applies a strict 5-minute rule the wait was still satisfied, but the driver did not document which threshold he counted against.

The driver's written statement (F14) that he waited "the full 8 minutes" is a party statement; the rider's account in the complaint (filed by rider) that she came out one minute after cancellation is also uncorroborated — the court may treat both as claims, though the GPS/timeline records (F2, F3, F6, F7) side with the driver's account.

NS-1's call element requires an in-app call: F13 shows the call was "not answered" and there is no recording, so if the court reads the element as requiring a connected call rather than an attempted one, the condition could be found unmet and the $5.00 voided under NS-2 — arguing against my own client's position, the record is unambiguous that the call was placed (F5, F13).

The driver cancelled at 17:22:55, 10 min 55 s after acceptance (F4); the rider may argue the driver could have waited once more given he had already signalled he was cancelling at 17:22 (F11), a timing point that cannot be settled from the records.

points.response: Conceded: F1/F2/F3 do establish arrival within 200 m, so NS-1(i) is met and I do not contest it.
Conceded: F7 shows the 'I'm Here' tap at 17:15:05, 40 m out, with 7 min 50 s continuously inside 200 m, so NS-1(iv) is met and no TH-4 escalation for a GPS gap arises.

Disputed: D3 asserts the wait was 'past the later-of-two wait on any reading', but the record's 8-minute threshold (NS-1(ii)) is measured at 7 min 50 s from arrival (F6, F3) and the record contains no scheduled pickup time to count from, so on the only clock the policy permits (later of scheduled time and arrival) the threshold is not shown to have passed before cancellation.
Conceded: F5 and F13 show 2 in-app messages (first 17:15:35) and 1 in-app call placed at 17:16:35 before cancellation at 17:22:55, so NS-1(iii) is satisfied on the record.

Partly conceded, but the same message defeats D5's point: F11 reads '8 min up, cancelling the trip' at 17:22, i.e. the driver announced the 8 minutes were only then up and cancelled at 17:22:55 — 7 min 50 s after his own 17:15:05 arrival (F7, F3) — so his own notice is short of the threshold he invoked.

Conceded that the app reason is rider_no_show and no errand is shown, so NS-3 is not the route; the issue is narrower — whether the NS-1 wait condition was actually met, and F14's 'waited the full 8 minutes' is a party statement contradicted by the 7 min 50 s record (F3, F6, F7), which wins.

Conceded that no record shows the rider approaching or messaging, so the complaint's 'one minute after' is uncorroborated; but D7 does not save the fee, because the charge depends on the driver's own wait threshold being met, and the record shows it was not.
Disputed: the fee is not 'standing on an upheld record' — NS-2 voids the $5.00 whenever any NS-1 hold fails, and the wait hold in NS-1(ii) is not shown satisfied at cancellation 17:22:55 (F8, F4).
Conceded: the $5.00 sum is system-final under TH-1/TH-2 and I seek no human escalation — I ask for a refund of the fee, not a referral.

Conceded: the driver's 6.5-year profile (F19) is background and I rely on it for no finding; if anything, 1291 trips in 90 days with 1 upheld no-show dispute shows a recurring cancellation-wait practice rather than a reason to let the charge stand.
Accepted as stated — GPS puts the driver within 200 m from 17:14:35 and stationary 40 m from the pickup from 17:15:05 to cancellation, so the arrival element of NS-1 is met (F1, F2, F3).
Not contested: the driver's presence is unbroken in the records, so NS-1(iv) is satisfied and the rider's TH-4 missing-GPS argument has nothing to attach to (F6, F7, F2).
Conceded: the rider's own brief accepts that 2 messages (first 17:15:35) and 1 call (17:16:35) were made before the 17:22:55 cancellation, which is exactly NS-1(iii) (F5, F13).

The clock is not undecidable: the driver was stationary at the pickup from 17:15:05 and cancelled 7 min 50 s later at 17:22:55, so on the record's 8-minute threshold the wait was met and at worst a reviewer reads a 10-second shortfall against a later scheduled pickup time — a margin that cannot support a full refund when the driver first reached the pickup at 17:14:35 and had been waiting since then (F2, F3, F6, F4).

The statement and the records agree on the substance — the driver arrived at the pickup, waited and cancelled for no-show; the "full 8 minutes" is at most an imprecision of ten seconds measured from arrival, and it does not create the driver-side reason the rider needs, since the app reason recorded is rider_no_show (F14, F4, F6, F7).

The 17:22 message reads as notice of intent to cancel at the expiry of the wait, not as an admission the wait had not expired: the driver sent it and then cancelled 55 seconds later, and the timeline records rider_no_show as the reason, so nothing in F11 converts this into an NS-3 driver-reason cancel (F11, F4, F14, F5).

The refund rests on a timing gap the rider's own brief calls undecidable and that the record does not establish; where the arrival, presence, message and call elements are all recorded and the charge is the fixed $5.00 no-surge fee, no part of the fee fails NS-1 and no refund is due under NS-2 (F8, F9, F5, F6, F7).

The rider's own profile shows 1 dispute in 90 days and none upheld, and the driver's single upheld matter is background only; a profile fact can never decide this case, and the rider's request that it be used "rather than any penalty on the rider" cuts against any account flag on either side (F18, F19).
Withdrawn as an independent claim — the opponent's C1 concedes arrival within 200 m and the point now stands as agreed between the sides (F1, F2, F3).

Restated, not withdrawn: because NS-1(i), (iii) and (iv) are now common ground and the only argued failure is a wait-condition timing point the rider calls undecidable, the fixed $5.00 fee with no surge (1.0×) should stand under NS-1/NS-2 (F8, F9, F5, F6, F13).

notices.text: We reviewed your no-show cancellation fee and you're getting a full refund of $5.00. The fee was charged after your driver cancelled, but the record shows he cancelled just before the required waiting time was up, so the fee doesn't apply. The $5.00 goes back to your original payment method; timing depends on your bank or card issuer. Nothing changes on your account — no flag, no impact on how you use Ryde.

We reviewed the $5.00 no-show fee you charged on this trip and it's being refunded to the rider in full. The arrival and contact steps were fine, but the record shows the cancellation came about ten seconds before the required waiting time was up, and a fee only stands if the full wait is completed. The $5.00 goes back to the rider's original payment method. A note goes on your record that the wait threshold wasn't reached; no account flag, and nothing else changes for you.
